whatis.intro: Warehouse capacity is how much stock a building can hold once aisles, dock and office are taken out. It is best counted in cases, through pallet positions and stack height. Square feet on a lease is only where the count starts.

cards.title: Three units, one building
cards.body: Square feet is the landlord's unit, pallet positions are the warehouse's, and cases are the buyer's. Capacity means the last one: 12,400 cases here.
cards.alt: Open book, for square feet, positions and cases

cards.title: What full really means
cards.body: The ceiling assumes every position is filled. Receiving needs open slots to put product away, so a working building runs below it.
cards.alt: Warning sign, for the open slots a working building needs

cards.title: Dated stock takes extra room
cards.body: Food ships oldest first, so a new delivery often cannot go in front of older stock. One item can then hold two positions at once.
cards.alt: Light bulb, for dated stock that needs a second position

who.h2: Who uses a warehouse size calculator
who.intro: Warehouse and operations managers at distributors reach for it when the question is what today's building holds. Anyone buying a bulk deal, booking a big inbound load or pricing new racking should check it.

look.h2: Before you plan a buy around capacity
look.intro: Capacity is only as true as the building figure and the flow you enter. A buyer planning against it should confirm each of these.

steps.title: The floor, not the lease
steps.body: A lease can measure to the outside of the walls, so measure the floor itself before you enter 3,000. Leave the office in it: the 55% usable share already takes the office out.

steps.title: Cases a pallet across the range
steps.body: The default of 50 cases a pallet will not fit every line. Bulky lines such as paper goods pallet far fewer, so weight the average by what sits on your racks.

steps.title: Throughput that never sits on a rack
steps.body: Weeks of cover divides capacity by every case you move. Leave out product that arrives and leaves the same day, or cover looks shorter than it is.

vos.h2: Where VOS fits, and where it stops
vos.h3: The cases you move start as orders
vos.body: VOS does not measure your building or run your warehouse. It sits on the order side: every order placed by voice in the VOS app arrives with a number, date and timestamp. Those dated app orders give one check on the monthly cases you enter.
